title: Cold-Crash Duration and Clarity Readiness
dataSources: Fermentation telemetry (`brew:fermentation`), brew-day records (`brew:batch`), mash probes (`brew:mash`), keg pressure (`kegerator:pressure`), tap pours (`kegerator:pour`), brew-fridge duty logs (`brewfridge:compressor`), cellar climate (`winecellar:reading`), and line-cleaning events (`tapline:clean`).
app: Homebrewing telemetry from Tilt/iSpindel fermentation sensors, Brewfather batch exports, ESPHome mash and fridge probes, keg pressure sensors, tap flow meters, and cellar climate sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation
| stats latest(cold_crash_hours) as cold_crash_hours latest(turbidity_ntu) as turbidity_ntu by batch
| eval readiness=if(cold_crash_hours>=24 AND turbidity_ntu<25,"ready","wait")
| sort readiness batch
description: Tracks how long each batch has been cold-crashing and whether the clarity trend suggests packaging readiness.
value: Packaging too early leaves haze and sediment behind, so a simple readiness view saves guesswork at the end of the process.
implementation: Capture cold-crash start times and periodic turbidity estimates from sensors or manual check-ins.
visualization: Status table of cold-crash hours, turbidity, and readiness.
grandmaExplanation: It logs whether the beer has chilled long enough to clear up before you package it.
